newsitem.title: USA: US senator says L.A. mayor diverted airport funds.
newsitem.headline: US senator says L.A. mayor diverted airport funds.

text.p: A U.S. senator charged Monday that Los Angeles Mayor Richard Riordan diverted more than $31 million in federal airport funds to the city hours before Congress voted to bar such moves by localities.

Sen. John McCain, R-Ariz., said in a two-page letter to Riordon that the mayor improperly diverted U.S. funds targeted for Los Angeles International Airport to pay city police and firefighters and other bills.
Riordan's office had no immediate response.
"The middle-of-the-night scheme circumvents" the spirit of a federal aviation bill approved by Congress Oct 3, said McCain, chairman of the aviation subpanel of the Senate Commerce Committee.
"The city's action will not fool anyone," McCain said, adding he will ask Secretary of Transportation Federico Pena to "use all all authority he has" to resolve the situation.
McCain said if Los Angeles does not return the $31 million, he will push to have the city's federal airport funding slashed by that amount.
John Driscoll, executive director of Los Angeles Department of Airports, defended the fund transfer.

"Under the eyes of our city attorney, it was determined to be a legal transfer," said Driscoll. "But independent of legal advice, they (the Los Angeles City Council) can still say they're not going to take that money. They can send it back."
Title 8 of airport bill, which President Clinton is expected to sign this week, strengthens federal laws that bar municipalities from diverting federal airport dollars.
Under the bill, Federal Aviation Reauthorization Act of 1996, cities can ask the federal government to reimburse them for contributions they have made to airports for the past six years.
Mayor Riordan contends the federal government owes L.A. millions of dollars for city purchases of airport land dating back 70 years ago, McCain's office said.
McCain first introduced language in May to reverse what he called an "alarming" trend by localities to divert airport dollars for non-airport purposes.
He said over $170 million has been diverted by at least 23 airport sponsors between 1992 and 1995, according to a recent audit by the inspector general of the Transportation Dept.
McCain called "reprehensible" the "blatant disregard" by cities like Los Angeles for federal laws that bar municipal governments from diverting revenues tagged for airports.
"Far too many local governments are attempting to solve their fiscal problems by taking money away from their airports, and using it for non-airport purposes," McCain said in May.
